- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) or mixed with sharp drops, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% to compensate.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak.  
- If model shows strong upward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive rising values) but sentiment is neutral or negative, reduce slope or add downward correction.  
- Mean reversion is strong in 3–5 day horizon: if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating highs/lows (e.g., 0.67, 0.33, 0.67…), model often misreads momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 values for smoothing.  
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is >10% above true outcome in 2+ consecutive days, apply “lag correction” — reduce by 0.5–1% per day until alignment.
